paragraphs: In Sutton, children in care live with carers approved by the council's fostering service or by independent agencies such as those listed on this page. The council says it is short of carers for young people aged 11 to 17, for sibling groups and for children with disabilities. It also looks for respite carers who can help at weekends, in school holidays and in emergencies, and short breaks carers who give regular support to disabled children living with their own families.

Sutton welcomes single people and couples, people who are working, not working or retired, and people of any ethnic, faith or LGBTQ+ background. You need to be over 21, with a spare room; there is no upper age limit, but you need to be fit and healthy. After you register interest, the council aims to reply within 24 hours. A social worker visits, then there are medical and DBS checks for adults in the household, a three-day Skills to Foster course and an assessment report for the fostering panel. The council says the process can take up to 16 weeks, and carers already approved elsewhere can transfer.

Approved carers have a supervising social worker, 24-hour access to the emergency duty team, therapeutic support, local support groups and social events, and a mentor who is an experienced Sutton carer during their first year. The council describes its pay as an allowance and fee package with additional payments, set out in a separate leaflet, so ask for the current figures.
Compare the council with two or three of the agencies below before you decide.
